# tidyvars

> A tidy interface for VAR models fitted with
> [vars](https://www.pfaffikus.de).

`tidyvars` makes results from Vector Autoregressive (VAR) models easier
to inspect, manipulate and visualize.

The package does not replace [vars](https://www.pfaffikus.de) or
reimplement VAR econometrics. [vars](https://www.pfaffikus.de) performs
the statistical calculations; `tidyvars` organizes the results into
consistent tidy objects that work naturally with
[dplyr](https://dplyr.tidyverse.org),
[tidyr](https://tidyr.tidyverse.org), and
[ggplot2](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org).

## Installation

`tidyvars` is currently under development. The `tv_2.0` version can be
installed from GitHub with [pak](https://pak.r-lib.org/):

``` r

devtools::install_github("Reckziegel/tidyvars")
```

## Quick start

Model estimation stays exactly where it belongs: in
[vars](https://www.pfaffikus.de).

``` r

library(tidyvars)
library(ggplot2)

model <- vars::VAR(
  EuStockMarkets,
  p = 2,
  type = "const"
)
```

From this point on, `tidyvars` provides a consistent interface for
working with the fitted model.

## Inspect model results

A fitted [vars](https://www.pfaffikus.de) model contains several
equation-specific and nested objects. `tidyvars` turns the most common
results into tidy tables.

``` r

tv_tidy(model)
#> <tidyvars coefficients>
#> Equations: 4 | Terms: 9
#> # A tibble: 36 × 6
#>    equation term    estimate std_error statistic   p_value
#>    <chr>    <chr>      <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>
#>  1 DAX      DAX.l1    0.996     0.0420    23.7   7.67e-109
#>  2 DAX      SMI.l1   -0.102     0.0293    -3.47  5.26e-  4
#>  3 DAX      CAC.l1    0.0468    0.0458     1.02  3.07e-  1
#>  4 DAX      FTSE.l1   0.0927    0.0360     2.58  1.01e-  2
#>  5 DAX      DAX.l2   -0.0219    0.0419    -0.522 6.01e-  1
#>  6 DAX      SMI.l2    0.117     0.0293     3.98  7.18e-  5
#>  7 DAX      CAC.l2   -0.0373    0.0460    -0.811 4.17e-  1
#>  8 DAX      FTSE.l2  -0.0925    0.0361    -2.56  1.05e-  2
#>  9 DAX      const    -3.67     13.4       -0.275 7.84e-  1
#> 10 SMI      DAX.l1    0.0119    0.0517     0.230 8.18e-  1
#> # ℹ 26 more rows

tv_glance(model)
#> <tidyvars equation summaries>
#> Equations: 4
#> # A tibble: 4 × 13
#>   equation r_squared adj_r_squared sigma statistic p_value    df log_lik    aic
#>   <chr>        <dbl>         <dbl> <dbl>     <dbl>   <dbl> <dbl>   <dbl>  <dbl>
#> 1 DAX          0.999         0.999  32.2   262882.       0     8  -9084. 18189.
#> 2 SMI          0.999         0.999  39.7   407363.       0     8  -9471. 18962.
#> 3 CAC          0.998         0.998  26.1   114737.       0     8  -8691. 17402.
#> 4 FTSE         0.999         0.999  30.2   242423.       0     8  -8964. 17948.
#> # ℹ 4 more variables: bic <dbl>, deviance <dbl>, df_residual <int>, n_obs <int>

tv_augment(model)
#> <tidyvars augmented data>
#> Variables: 4 | Observations: 1860
#> # A tibble: 7,440 × 5
#>    index variable observed fitted residual
#>    <dbl> <chr>       <dbl>  <dbl>    <dbl>
#>  1 1991. DAX         1629.    NA     NA   
#>  2 1991. SMI         1678.    NA     NA   
#>  3 1991. CAC         1773.    NA     NA   
#>  4 1991. FTSE        2444.    NA     NA   
#>  5 1992. DAX         1614.    NA     NA   
#>  6 1992. SMI         1688.    NA     NA   
#>  7 1992. CAC         1750.    NA     NA   
#>  8 1992. FTSE        2460.    NA     NA   
#>  9 1992. DAX         1607.  1609.    -2.66
#> 10 1992. SMI         1679.  1687.    -8.86
#> # ℹ 7,430 more rows
```

[`tv_tidy()`](https://github.com/Reckziegel/tidyvars/reference/tv_tidy.md)
returns coefficient estimates by equation,
[`tv_glance()`](https://github.com/Reckziegel/tidyvars/reference/tv_glance.md)
provides equation-level summaries, and
[`tv_augment()`](https://github.com/Reckziegel/tidyvars/reference/tv_augment.md)
aligns observed values, fitted values, and residuals.

The outputs use predictable lower-case `snake_case` column names while
preserving the original variable names from the model.

Because the results are tidy, they can immediately enter a normal
tidyverse workflow:

``` r

model |>
  tv_tidy() |>
  dplyr::filter(p_value < 0.05) |>
  dplyr::select(equation, term, estimate, p_value)
#> <tidyvars coefficients>
#> Equations: 4 | Terms: 7
#> # A tibble: 18 × 4
#>    equation term    estimate   p_value
#>    <chr>    <chr>      <dbl>     <dbl>
#>  1 DAX      DAX.l1    0.996  7.67e-109
#>  2 DAX      SMI.l1   -0.102  5.26e-  4
#>  3 DAX      FTSE.l1   0.0927 1.01e-  2
#>  4 DAX      SMI.l2    0.117  7.18e-  5
#>  5 DAX      FTSE.l2  -0.0925 1.05e-  2
#>  6 SMI      SMI.l1    0.962  9.57e-133
#>  7 SMI      FTSE.l1   0.145  1.10e-  3
#>  8 SMI      FTSE.l2  -0.131  3.15e-  3
#>  9 CAC      SMI.l1   -0.0713 2.68e-  3
#> 10 CAC      CAC.l1    1.04   4.93e-144
#> 11 CAC      FTSE.l1   0.0840 3.98e-  3
#> 12 CAC      SMI.l2    0.0834 4.48e-  4
#> 13 CAC      FTSE.l2  -0.0895 2.24e-  3
#> 14 FTSE     SMI.l1   -0.0912 9.15e-  4
#> 15 FTSE     FTSE.l1   1.18   3.37e-207
#> 16 FTSE     SMI.l2    0.109  7.14e-  5
#> 17 FTSE     FTSE.l2  -0.199  4.89e-  9
#> 18 FTSE     const    39.2    1.78e-  3
```

There is no need to navigate `model$varresult`, combine equation outputs
manually, or reshape them before analysis.

## Dynamic analysis

Impulse response functions and forecast error variance decompositions
follow the same pattern.

``` r

set.seed(123)

irf <- tv_irf(model)
fevd <- tv_fevd(model)
```

An impulse response can be inspected directly as data:

``` r

irf |>
  dplyr::filter(
    impulse == "DAX",
    response == "SMI"
  )
#> <tidyvars IRF>
#> Impulses: 1 | Responses: 1 | Horizons: 0-10
#> # A tibble: 11 × 6
#>    horizon impulse response estimate lower upper
#>      <int> <chr>   <chr>       <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>
#>  1       0 DAX     SMI          29.8  26.9  33.0
#>  2       1 DAX     SMI          32.7  29.7  36.7
#>  3       2 DAX     SMI          32.9  29.7  36.6
#>  4       3 DAX     SMI          32.8  29.7  36.3
#>  5       4 DAX     SMI          32.8  29.6  36.1
#>  6       5 DAX     SMI          32.8  29.6  36.0
#>  7       6 DAX     SMI          32.8  29.6  35.9
#>  8       7 DAX     SMI          32.7  29.5  35.9
#>  9       8 DAX     SMI          32.7  29.5  35.9
#> 10       9 DAX     SMI          32.7  29.5  35.9
#> 11      10 DAX     SMI          32.6  29.4  35.9
```

Each row identifies the horizon, impulse, response, estimate, and
confidence interval.

The same object can be plotted directly:

``` r

autoplot(irf, layout = "wrap") +
  theme_tidyvars() +
  palette_tidyvars()
```

![](reference/figures/README-irf-plot-1.png)

FEVD results are also returned in tidy form, with one contribution for
each horizon, response, and shock:

``` r

autoplot(fevd) +
  theme_tidyvars() +
  palette_tidyvars()
```

![](reference/figures/README-fevd-plot-1.png)

Conceptually:

``` text
IRF  → response to a shock through time
FEVD → contribution of each shock to forecast uncertainty
```

Both objects can be filtered, transformed, joined, or plotted using
standard tidyverse tools.

## Forecasting

[`tv_predict()`](https://github.com/Reckziegel/tidyvars/reference/tv_predict.md)
converts forecasts from [vars](https://www.pfaffikus.de) into a single
tidy object containing historical observations, point forecasts, and
confidence intervals.

Multiple confidence levels can be requested at once:

``` r

prediction <- tv_predict(
  model,
  n_ahead = 12,
  level = c(0.50, 0.75, 0.90)
)

prediction
#> <tidyvars forecast>
#> Variables: 4 | History: 1860 | Forecast: 12
#> # A tibble: 7,584 × 8
#>    index variable type    level observed estimate lower upper
#>    <dbl> <chr>    <chr>   <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>
#>  1 1991. DAX      history    NA    1629.       NA    NA    NA
#>  2 1991. SMI      history    NA    1678.       NA    NA    NA
#>  3 1991. CAC      history    NA    1773.       NA    NA    NA
#>  4 1991. FTSE     history    NA    2444.       NA    NA    NA
#>  5 1992. DAX      history    NA    1614.       NA    NA    NA
#>  6 1992. SMI      history    NA    1688.       NA    NA    NA
#>  7 1992. CAC      history    NA    1750.       NA    NA    NA
#>  8 1992. FTSE     history    NA    2460.       NA    NA    NA
#>  9 1992. DAX      history    NA    1607.       NA    NA    NA
#> 10 1992. SMI      history    NA    1679.       NA    NA    NA
#> # ℹ 7,574 more rows
```

The result can be plotted directly:

``` r

autoplot(prediction, n_history = 30) +
  theme_tidyvars() +
  palette_tidyvars()
```

![](reference/figures/README-forecast-plot-1.png)

`n_history` controls only how much historical context is displayed. The
forecast horizon itself is never truncated.

As with the other `tidyvars` objects, the forecast remains available as
ordinary tidy data for further manipulation.

## Diagnostics

Common VAR diagnostics are exposed through the same tabular interface:

``` r

tv_causality(model)
#> <tidyvars causality tests>
#> Causes: 4 | Tests: 2
#> # A tibble: 8 × 9
#>   cause test          statistic    df   df1   df2 boot_runs   p_value method    
#>   <chr> <chr>             <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl> <chr>     
#> 1 DAX   granger           0.895    NA     6  7396        NA 0.497     Granger c…
#> 2 DAX   instantaneous   763.        3    NA    NA        NA 0         H0: No in…
#> 3 SMI   granger           4.70     NA     6  7396        NA 0.0000874 Granger c…
#> 4 SMI   instantaneous   691.        3    NA    NA        NA 0         H0: No in…
#> 5 CAC   granger           3.79     NA     6  7396        NA 0.000899  Granger c…
#> 6 CAC   instantaneous   702.        3    NA    NA        NA 0         H0: No in…
#> 7 FTSE  granger           3.86     NA     6  7396        NA 0.000750  Granger c…
#> 8 FTSE  instantaneous   647.        3    NA    NA        NA 0         H0: No in…

tv_normality_test(model)
#> <tidyvars normality tests>
#> Scopes: 1 | Tests: 3
#> # A tibble: 3 × 7
#>   scope        variable test        statistic    df p_value method              
#>   <chr>        <chr>    <chr>           <dbl> <dbl>   <dbl> <chr>               
#> 1 multivariate <NA>     jarque_bera     9979.     8       0 JB-Test (multivaria…
#> 2 multivariate <NA>     skewness         146.     4       0 Skewness only (mult…
#> 3 multivariate <NA>     kurtosis        9832.     4       0 Kurtosis only (mult…

tv_serial_test(model)
#> <tidyvars serial tests>
#> Tests: 1
#> # A tibble: 1 × 8
#>   test                    lags statistic    df   df1   df2 p_value method       
#>   <chr>                  <int>     <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>   <dbl> <chr>        
#> 1 portmanteau_asymptotic    16      463.   224    NA    NA       0 Portmanteau …
```

These functions organize the corresponding results from
[vars](https://www.pfaffikus.de) rather than reimplementing the
underlying statistical tests.

The returned tables use normalized identifiers and predictable schemas,
making diagnostic results easy to filter, compare or include in reports.

## Visualization

`tidyvars` provides
[`autoplot()`](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/autoplot.html)
methods for IRFs, FEVDs, and forecasts.

The plotting methods define the structure of the visualization but do
not impose the visual identity of the package.

A `tidyvars` plot is still a regular `ggplot` object:

``` r

autoplot(irf) +
  ggplot2::theme_classic()
```

The optional visual system separates layout from colour:

``` r

autoplot(irf) +
  theme_tidyvars() +
  palette_tidyvars()
```

``` text
theme_tidyvars()   → layout and typography
palette_tidyvars() → colours
```

[`theme_tidyvars()`](https://github.com/Reckziegel/tidyvars/reference/theme_tidyvars.md)
controls structural elements such as typography, spacing, grids, facets,
and legends without changing the colours used for the data.

[`palette_tidyvars()`](https://github.com/Reckziegel/tidyvars/reference/palette_tidyvars.md)
applies the package colour identity only when explicitly requested.

Discrete scales are also available independently for ordinary ggplot2
graphics:

``` r

scale_color_tidyvars()
scale_fill_tidyvars()
```

This keeps the visual system optional and fully compatible with normal
ggplot2 customization.

# Package index

## Tidiers

- [`tv_tidy()`](https://github.com/Reckziegel/tidyvars/reference/tv_tidy.md)
  : Tidy VAR model coefficients
- [`tv_glance()`](https://github.com/Reckziegel/tidyvars/reference/tv_glance.md)
  : Glance at the equations of a VAR model
- [`tv_augment()`](https://github.com/Reckziegel/tidyvars/reference/tv_augment.md)
  : Augment a VAR model

## Tests

- [`tv_normality_test()`](https://github.com/Reckziegel/tidyvars/reference/tv_normality_test.md)
  : Tidy VAR normality tests
- [`tv_serial_test()`](https://github.com/Reckziegel/tidyvars/reference/tv_serial_test.md)
  : Tidy VAR serial correlation test
- [`tv_causality()`](https://github.com/Reckziegel/tidyvars/reference/tv_causality.md)
  : Tidy causality tests

## Forecasting

- [`tv_predict()`](https://github.com/Reckziegel/tidyvars/reference/tv_predict.md)
  : Tidy VAR forecasts

## Inference

- [`tv_irf()`](https://github.com/Reckziegel/tidyvars/reference/tv_irf.md)
  : Tidy impulse-response functions
- [`tv_fevd()`](https://github.com/Reckziegel/tidyvars/reference/tv_fevd.md)
  : Tidy forecast error variance decomposition

## Plotting

- [`autoplot(`*`<tv_irf>`*`)`](https://github.com/Reckziegel/tidyvars/reference/autoplot.tv_irf.md)
  : Autoplot tidyvars objects
- [`autoplot(`*`<tv_fevd>`*`)`](https://github.com/Reckziegel/tidyvars/reference/autoplot.tv_fevd.md)
  : Autoplot FEVD results
- [`autoplot(`*`<tv_predict>`*`)`](https://github.com/Reckziegel/tidyvars/reference/autoplot.tv_predict.md)
  : Autoplot forecast results
- [`palette_tidyvars()`](https://github.com/Reckziegel/tidyvars/reference/palette_tidyvars.md)
  : tidyvars colour palette
- [`scale_color_tidyvars()`](https://github.com/Reckziegel/tidyvars/reference/scale_color_tidyvars.md)
  [`scale_fill_tidyvars()`](https://github.com/Reckziegel/tidyvars/reference/scale_color_tidyvars.md)
  : tidyvars discrete colour scales
- [`theme_tidyvars()`](https://github.com/Reckziegel/tidyvars/reference/theme_tidyvars.md)
  : tidyvars ggplot2 theme
